title: User secrets, environment variables, and Azure Key Vault
hook: Secrets never belong in git — user secrets protect local development, environment variables inject container settings, and Azure Key Vault is the production vault for connection strings, API keys, and signing certificates.

blocks.text: The Secret Manager tool (user secrets) stores key-value pairs outside the project tree in a user profile folder, loaded only when EnvironmentName is Development. Environment variables are the standard production transport in Docker and Kubernetes — map ConnectionStrings__OrdersDb to the connection string. Azure Key Vault configuration provider pulls secrets at startup using managed identity or service principal, optionally with reload intervals. Each is a configuration provider in the same merge chain.

entries.plainDefinition: Local-only secret store per project. Not deployed. Enabled via UserSecretsId in csproj.
Cloud secret and certificate store. ASP.NET Core provider maps vault secrets to configuration keys.
Azure-assigned identity for the app without storing credentials in code. DefaultAzureCredential uses it in Azure.
entries.example: App Service / AKS pod identity accesses Key Vault without client secret.

entries.plainDefinition: Chained credential that tries env vars, managed identity, Azure CLI, and Visual Studio login in order.
entries.example: Works locally with az login and in Azure with managed identity.

blocks.text: Committed secrets in appsettings.json are scanned by bots within minutes — credential rotation and incident response follow. Production Web APIs in Azure, AWS, or Kubernetes must source secrets from vaults or orchestrator secret objects, never from the image layer. Senior interviews ask how you rotate JWT signing keys, how Key Vault integrates with configuration reload, and why user secrets are not a deployment mechanism.

blocks.title: Secrets in production hierarchy
blocks.body: Preferred order: Azure Key Vault (or cloud equivalent) → Kubernetes secrets as env vars → never plain text in appsettings committed to git. User secrets are Development-only.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Local Development
items.body: dotnet user-secrets init; set values via CLI. Loaded after appsettings.Development.json.

items.title: Container / K8s
items.body: Secrets mounted as env vars or files. Env var provider maps __ to configuration keys.

items.title: Azure production
items.body: AddAzureKeyVault with managed identity. Vault secret names use -- instead of : (Jwt--SigningKey).

items.title: Validation at startup
items.body: ValidateOnStart ensures secrets exist and meet length/format rules before serving.

snippet.label: User secrets CLI workflow
snippet.code:
# One-time per project
dotnet user-secrets init

# Set secrets (colon in key name)
dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:OrdersDb" "Server=localhost;Database=Orders"
dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:SigningKey" "local-dev-key-min-32-chars-long!!"

# List (values shown in dev only)
dotnet user-secrets list
snippet.explanation: UserSecretsId in csproj links project to secret store. Values live in ~/.microsoft/usersecrets/{id}/secrets.json — never in the repo.

snippet.label: Azure Key Vault configuration provider
snippet.explanation: Key Vault URI often in appsettings (non-secret). DefaultAzureCredential uses managed identity in Azure and az login locally. Secret names use -- delimiter.

snippet.label: Kubernetes secret as environment variable
snippet.code:
# deployment.yaml excerpt
env:
  - name: ConnectionStrings__OrdersDb
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: orders-api-secrets
        key: orders-db-connection
  - name: Jwt__SigningKey
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: orders-api-secrets
        key: jwt-signing-key
snippet.explanation: K8s secret keys map to env var names with double underscore. ASP.NET Core configuration provider reads them like any other env var — no code changes needed.

snippet.label: Never log secret values — diagnostic pattern
snippet.explanation: Health checks verify secrets exist without exposing them. Application Insights and structured logs must redact connection strings — use ILogger redaction or custom enricher.

blocks.title: Secret management patterns
rows: AWS Secrets Manager / env from K8s
Key Vault provider or K8s env vars
User secrets never in project folder

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Committing appsettings.Development.json with real passwords. Deploying user secrets — they are not packaged. Key Vault secret named Jwt:SigningKey (colon invalid) — use Jwt--SigningKey. Logging IConfiguration dump in production. Storing service principal client secret in appsettings instead of managed identity.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: enable Azure Key Vault diagnostic logs — audit secret Get operations correlated with app startup and reload events. Rotate Jwt:SigningKey in Key Vault with dual-key acceptance window — IOptionsMonitor.OnChange or pod rolling restart depending on reload config. Scan git history with gitleaks or GitHub secret scanning. K8s: verify secrets are mounted as env vars not baked into container images (docker history). For AWS, Parameter Store or Secrets Manager integrate via similar configuration providers or env injection.

blocks.title: Secret storage tradeoffs
rows: Thinking they deploy with the app
Base64 in etcd — enable encryption at rest
Startup latency; cache with reload interval
Visible in portal to admins — audit access
Local dev needs az login or dev credential

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Storing production connection strings in appsettings.json. Not knowing user secrets are Development-only. Unable to explain Key Vault secret naming (-- vs :). Saying secrets in environment variables are 'secure enough' without mentioning who can read pod env in K8s.

interviewTakeaways: User secrets for local dev; environment variables for containers; Key Vault for Azure production secrets.
Key Vault secret names use -- instead of :; K8s env vars use __ for hierarchical keys.
Production tip: managed identity to Key Vault — no client secrets in config; rotate keys with reload or rolling deploy.
60s: Never commit secrets. User secrets local only. K8s secrets as env vars with __. Key Vault via AddAzureKeyVault and DefaultAzureCredential. ValidateOnStart ensures presence.
Follow-up: how do you rotate JWT signing keys without downtime?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'user secrets work in production' gets you rejected — they are not deployed and exist only on the developer machine.
Logging configuration with GetDebugView in production — may expose secret values.
Strong answer: 'Dev: user secrets. Prod: Key Vault with managed identity or K8s secrets as env vars. ValidateOnStart, never log values, rotate via vault versioning.'
introducedIn: User secrets in ASP.NET Core 1.0; Azure Key Vault provider in Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.AzureKeyVault

jsTsCorrelations.note: .env lives in project (gitignored) — still risk of accidental commit. User secrets store outside the repo entirely. Both load into a key-value config model.
Cloud secret managers integrate similarly — fetch at startup into process.env or ConfigService. ASP.NET Key Vault provider merges into IConfiguration natively.
